title: Eval & Quality Monitoring Demo - Solace Finance
summary: Redwood demo focused on the Eval / Quality Monitoring features: prompt set management, regression alerts, and A/B comparison workflows. Customer is evaluating regression detection for model rollouts and wants to run A/B experiments between quantized and full models. Security and data retention questions raised; agreed to share security pack and evaluation spreadsheet. Next step: send pricing + trial instructions and schedule a 2-week pilot kickoff.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood Product), Liam (Solace Head of ML), Priya (Eng Manager), Dana (Product), Omar (Sec Ops)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, uh, I'll kick us off. This is an Eval and Quality Monitoring walkthrough, we'll cover prompt sets, regression alerts and A over B workflows in Redwood Optimize and the Console. Ethan will run the demo.
[00:12] Liam: Great, thanks, Maya. Quick note - we're focused on model rollouts for customer-facing summarization, want to catch regressions early.
[00:20] Priya: And we have strict latency SLOs, so any QA needs to factor that in.
[00:28] Ethan: Got it. Quick agenda: 1) how to onboard prompt sets, 2) setting automated regression alerts, 3) A/B runbooks and dashboards, 4) integration notes.
[01:05] Ethan: I'll share my screen  okay, can everyone see the Console?
[01:09] Dana: Yep, seeing it.
[01:22] Ethan: So here is the Eval dashboard. You can create a 'prompt set' which is basically a curated corpus of prompts + expected outputs or metrics. We support both golden outputs and metric-based assertions like rouge, exact-match, BLEU, embedding-similarity.
[01:48] Liam: For summarization we mainly use ROUGE-L and an embedding-sim threshold for semantic drift. Can Redwood ingest our existing test harness? We have a junit-like CSV and a few annotation columns.
[01:58] Ethan: Yes, we have CSV import and a CI-friendly API. You can upload prompt sets via the API or the Console, and tie them to branches or model versions. The CSV mapping can be adjusted during import.
[02:20] Maya: Quick caveat: sometimes auto-detection mislabels columns if header names differ, but you can map them manually in the UI.
[02:35] Priya: Makes sense. About regression alerts, how are thresholds computed? Are they absolute or relative?
[02:42] Ethan: You can define absolute thresholds or relative regressions. For example, baseline ROUGE-L >= 0.35, and alert if new model drops by 5% relative. There are smoothing windows to avoid noise.
[03:08] Ethan: Demo: I'm configuring a regression alert tied to a model rollout job. I pick the prompt set 'Solace-summaries-q1', metric ROUGE-L, baseline mode set to 'canary baseline' from previous deployment.
[03:25] Maya: Also show the historical trend lines, right?
[03:28] Ethan: Yep. Here is the time-series. You can slice by customer segment, input length, and other metadata - this helps isolate regressions per cohort.
[03:52] Liam: Cohort slicing is huge for us. We care about long-form summaries > 512 tokens.
[03:58] Ethan: You can set filters on the prompt set items or attach tags during import.
[04:10] Sofia: Quick product note  we have a 'regression severity' classifier that can categorize alerts into 'minor', 'major', 'critical' based on metric deltas and query volume.
[04:25] Omar: On the security side, where is the prompt set stored and for how long? We need to avoid storing PII beyond retention windows.
[04:33] Ethan: Prompt sets can be stored in the Redwood control plane (encrypted at rest) or you can configure S3 with customer-managed KMS. Retention is configurable; we support automatic purge policies.
[04:50] Omar: And SOC 2? Audit logs?
[04:53] Maya: We are SOC 2 Type II, provide audit logs and SSO/SAML, RBAC. We'll send the security pack after this call.
[05:02] Priya: Good. Back to A/B -- we want to compare a quantized 4-bit variant vs the full float model, both behind same destination. Does Redwood support pairwise A/B with metric tracking?
[05:12] Ethan: Yes. In the rollout UI you can create an experiment: define variant A and variant B, assign traffic split, and pick evaluation windows. The system will evaluate metrics over the prompt set and produce statistical significance tests, lift charts, and per-prompt diffs.
[05:36] Liam: Can we do per-user bucketing or only deterministic hash?
[05:40] Ethan: We support deterministic bucketing by user-id, session-id, or custom key. You can also do geo and region constraints.
[05:49] Dana: Show an example report.
[05:52] Ethan: Here's a sample A/B report  difference in ROUGE-L with 95% CI, per-prompt examples where outputs differ, and a table of regression hits. You can drill into any row.
[06:20] Ethan: Note: when you compare quantized vs float there may be quality drift mostly on rare tokens; we surface token-level diffs and semantic similarity to help triage.
[06:36] Priya: That token-level diff view  is that generated via embeddings or exact token align?
[06:41] Ethan: Both. We produce token diff and embedding-based semantic similarity; the UI links to reference output and candidate outputs.
[06:52] Liam: For our internal process, we want automatic triage rules: if drift is > X and volume > Y then create a JIRA and assign to the model owner. Can Redwood integrate with JIRA?
[07:05] Ethan: Absolutely. We have webhooks and direct integrations  you can configure a workflow that creates tickets, sends Slack alerts, or hits an Ops runbook.
[07:18] Maya: I'll also note the 'quiet window' feature  avoid noisy alerts during deploy windows.
[07:27] Omar: About retention of logs used by the eval  are those separate from inference logs? Who can access them?
[07:34] Ethan: Access is governed by RBAC. Eval logs are stored per project and access controlled; if you use Private deployment, logs stay in your VPC.
[07:48] Liam: Any gotchas for latency when running A/B monitoring? We need near real-time detection but can't add significant token latency.
[07:56] Ethan: Monitoring is async for heavy compute (embedding comparisons), so it doesn't impact inference latency. For quick metrics we stream lightweight signals and compute heavier metrics offline.
[08:12] Priya: How fast is 'near real-time'?
[08:16] Ethan: Typical materialization is within 1-5 minutes depending on the metric and sample size.
[08:24] Liam: That's acceptable.
[08:30] Ethan: I'll demo uploading a prompt set. Watch the import wizard - you can map columns, set expected metrics, and attach metadata tags.
[09:02] [screen scrolls]
[09:15] Ethan: Upload complete. It detected language mismatches in two rows, flagged them as potential noise.
[09:25] Dana: Can we set up golden outputs with human annotations and accept a disagreement threshold?
[09:30] Ethan: Yes  annotation status and reviewer metadata are supported; you can set disagreement tolerances and fallback to human review if disagreement exceeds threshold.
[09:45] Priya: For the regression alerts, can we run a dry-run to see false-positive rate before enabling automatic tickets?
[09:54] Ethan: You can run backtests over historical deployments to estimate false positives and tune thresholds. We also provide suggestions based on your prompt set distribution.
[10:18] Liam: What about A/B statistical tests  do you support Bayesian tests or frequentist only?
[10:25] Ethan: We support both. Default is a frequentist t-test with correction, optional Bayesian analysis for small sample sizes.
[10:36] Omar: Do you preserve user identifiers in any of these datasets? We need pseudonymization.
[10:42] Ethan: You can configure pseudonymization on ingest; we support hashing and tokenization and can exclude PII fields.
[10:50] Maya: I'm going to switch to the API demo to show programmatic workflows for CI integration.
[10:55] Ethan: Here's how to POST a prompt set and trigger a regression check in CI: curl example, payload fields.
[11:08] Ethan: Note that we have SDK helper functions in Python and Node for uploading prompt sets, running comparisons, and fetching result summaries.
[11:20] Priya: We'll need the Python SDK  can you share code snippets?
[11:24] Maya: Yep, we'll include the SDK snippet in the follow up along with an example spreadsheet for imports.
[11:32] Liam: For a pilot, what's the minimal setup time? We have 2 weeks to run an internal eval before a larger rollout.
[11:40] Ethan: Minimal is 2-3 days to get a prompt set and baseline run, but for a robust pilot with A/B you should plan about 2 weeks. That matches your timeline.
[11:52] Dana: Any sample dashboards we can clone?
[11:55] Ethan: We can share a template dashboard and a sample prompt set.
[12:03] Priya: Can we scope a runbook: if major regression detected, rollback automatically to last stable model?
[12:12] Ethan: You can configure automatic rollback policies, or only open a canary gate  it's configurable per rollout.
[12:25] Sophia: Also note cost implications  computing heavy embedding diffs at high QPS increases cost; Redwood Optimize gives suggestions to sample intelligently to reduce cost while retaining sensitivity.
[12:37] Liam: Good  we need cost tradeoffs documented.
[12:42] Ethan: I'll show the sampling strategy  stratified sampling by input length and user cohort.
[13:00] [demo progressing, screen shows sampling configuration and thresholds]
[14:05] Priya: Who typically owns eval maintenance inside a customer org? Product or ML infra?
[14:12] Ethan: Customers vary; common pattern is ML infra owns pipelines and Product owns prompt set curation.
[14:25] Liam: We'll probably split it like that.
[14:30] Dana: Quick question from product: can we tag prompts as 'safety-sensitive' to exclude from public analytics?
[14:36] Ethan: Yes, tags and access controls let you exclude or mask data for specific items.
[14:45] Omar: For Private deployment, can we run the eval workers in our VPC to keep all artifacts internal?
[14:52] Ethan: Yes, for Private we provide an option to deploy evaluation workers in-customer VPC or on-prem so artifacts never leave your network.
[15:05] Liam: That would be our preference.
[15:10] Ethan: I'll mark that in notes.
[15:15] Maya: Let's walk through an example A/B that we've run internally that shows a subtle regression on long tail queries.
[15:22] Ethan: This example shows model B (quantized) drifting on rare named entities  we surface token diffs and an embedding-based similarity drop.
[15:33] Priya: Can the system automatically suggest which prompts to add to the prompt set to better surface that regression?
[15:40] Ethan: Yes  we have a suggestion engine that surfaces high-leverage prompts based on delta and volume.
[15:50] Liam: Ok great.
[16:00] [mid-call, 16:00 mark, participants ask clarifying Qs about API rate limits and batching]
[16:15] Ethan: Regarding rate limits: hosted tier has per-project quotas but Dedicated gives you reserved throughput. We can simulate load in a POC. Batching and KV cache settings influence latency.
[16:33] Priya: What's KV cache? I think you meant KV cache.
[16:36] Ethan: Yeah KV cache  sorry, my bad, it's the key-value cache.
[16:40] Liam: Any interplay between caching and regression detection?
[16:44] Ethan: Not directly; evaluation can be run on raw outputs before cache, or on served outputs depending on config.
[16:52] Omar: For evidence in audits, can we export a tamper-evident record of the evaluation runs?
[16:58] Ethan: We provide exportable artifacts with checksums and audit trails.
[17:08] Priya: Cool.
[17:15] [screen shows JIRA integration config]
[17:30] Maya: Okay, to wrap  we'll send the security packet, sample dashboard, SDK snippets, and the trial instructions. We'll also propose a pilot plan for two weeks.
[17:45] Liam: Sounds good. Two questions: 1) pricing for an initial pilot 2) can we run eval workers in our VPC?
[17:54] Maya: We'll include pricing ranges for hosted and private, and confirm deployment options for eval workers.
[18:05] Dana: Anything else on clustering or GPUs for heavy embedding workloads?
[18:12] Ethan: We can provision Dedicated capacity or run evaluation workers on CPU for lower cost; heavy embedding compute typically runs on GPU pools in Dedicated.
[18:27] Priya: Please include expected cost estimates for three sample volumes.
[18:33] Maya: Will do.
[18:40] [closing small talk, scheduling follow up]
[19:05] Maya: Thanks everyone  we'll follow up with the docs.
[19:12] Liam: Thanks all.
[19:20] [call ends]
